text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovak securities traders have criticised a new Finance Ministry draft law on collective investment, saying it could further damage investment in Slovakia.
- Major opposition parties still insist on the dismissal of Interior Minister Gustav Krajci before they start talks with the ruling coalition.
- The crown last week tested the parity level of its mark/dollar basket but dealers said the currency should not significantly move into the appreaciation side of the basket in the near future.
- Short-term interbank rates are expected to move between 24 to 30 percent this week.
- Rhodes Slovakia, a 100-percent subsidiary of Australian mining company Rhodes Mining NL Perth, has discovered gold resources worth some 500 million crowns near Detva, Northern Slovakia.

SME - President Michal Kovac said the U.S. decision to chose Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic for the first wave of NATO enlargement could bring stronger pressure on the government and Slovaks to convince the west that Bratislava belongs in the first round of NATO expansion.

- Five opposition parties -- Christian Democratic Movement (KDH), Democratic Union (DU), Democratic Party (DS), Social Democratic Party (SDSS) and the Green Party (SZS) -- have signed a coalition agreement for the next year's planned parliamentary elections.
PRAVDA - The downtrend on the Bratislava Stock Exchange is caused by uncertanity over the crown and insufficient protection of minority shareholders, analysts say.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Deputy Economics Minister Jan Foltin said Slovakia could be considering the re-introduction of import surchange if the EU said such a measure would be more appropriate tool to solve foreign trade problems than the current import deposits.
